business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (mainland territory, unitary corporate and AML registers)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–China Bilateral Investment Agreement (2005, in force 2008)
Spanish Bilateral Investment Treaties with 21 Latin American states, notably Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Peru
Spain–United States Double Taxation Convention (1999, amended by 2013 Protocol)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio), Articles 9-14, 19-22, 62, 124-136 and 138-142; Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996); Law 14/2013 for the Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for inscription; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for the tax identification number.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) and certified copy (primer testimonio) submitted for inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and paid-up capital: EUR 3,000, fully paid at formation. No escrow account is required; cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso). In-kind contributions require an independent expert report under Article 67 LSC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: 1. The share subscriptions of the incorporating shareholders are accepted; the subscribed capital is hereby fixed at EUR 3,000, fully paid in cash, and the bank certificate evidencing payment is approved. 2. The statutory articles are adopted verbatim; the registered office is fixed at [legal address], Spain, and the corporate purpose includes the international trading, recycling, storage and distribution of non-ferrous metal scrap, particularly shredded copper wire. 3. The shareholders appoint [Name] as Director and [Name] as Secretary, grant them the powers listed in Articles of Association, and authorise them to procure the provisional tax number, complete registry registrations and execute all pre-registration actions. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via the Ministry of Justice electronic portal, by fax, or through a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name reservation request with three proposed distinctive names and shareholder identification. If any name is accepted, the issued certificate is valid for three months, renewable for another three months, and must be attached to the notarial deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Application form for name certificate (solicitud de certificación de denominación social)
Passport/DNI/NIE of each promotor or shareholder
List of up to three preferred company names
Power of attorney if acting through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry refuses the name as identical or too similar to an existing one, submit a revised list of alternative names; if no response issues within the regulatory period, request accelerated certification or apply for a substitute name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) of the Notarial College in the seat of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, draft articles, bank certificate showing full payment of EUR 3,000 into an SL bank account, and proof of identity of all shareholders and directors. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the deed, and gives the first certified copy (testimonio) for registration.
required_dossiers: Certificado de denominación social (name certificate)
Bank certificate of capital deposit (certificado bancario de desembolso)
Draft Articles of Association (estatutos sociales)
Valid passport or NIE of every shareholder and appointed director
Auditor/expert report for non-cash contributions if applicable (Article 67 LSC)
Address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies invalid provisions, amend the statutes prior to execution; if the deed is executed with formal errors, execute a notarial corrective act before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF) and Tax Census Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Delegation of the province of the registered office / Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the deed to the AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF. Concurrently file Form 030/036 to register the company in the tax census, stating corporate purpose, registered office, activity code (CNAE 4669 / ISIC 4669), and directors. The provisional NIF is printed on the notarial deed and used for all subsequent steps.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed
Name certificate
Form 030/036 (census enrolment)
Identity details of all directors
Licence/activity code and estimated taxable operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT refuses or places the file in incident, correct the census data through the electronic office or submit a rectification application; the provisional NIF can be expedited by showing the deed and bank certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the company has its registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the previously notarized certified deed within 30 days of execution, together with proof of payment of the Documented Legal Acts tax (Modelo 600) and provisional NIF. The registrar verifies the legality of the deed and the identity of the subscribers, and issues the positive registration certificate, completing the legal personality of the company.
required_dossiers: First certified copy (testimonio) of the deed of incorporation
Original name certificate
Modelo 600 proof of tax payment
Form 030/036 copy and provisional NIF
Application for registration (instancia) if not filed electronically
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar notes defects, request correction by a notarial supplementary deed or by the registrar's note; if the defect remains, file an appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, Company Books, and Corporate Governance Formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Registro Mercantil Provincial for legalization of books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registry returns the certified registration, apply to the AEAT for the definitive NIF (CIF) using Form 030/036 and provide the registry certificate. Legalize the statutory books (book of shareholders, minutes book, inventory and annual accounts) at the Mercantile Registry or via its electronic office before physically using them. Hold statutory meetings and file signed consent resolutions as required.
required_dossiers: Registry certificate of inscription
Certified copy of the deed
Form 030/036 amendment to convert provisional NIF to definitive
DNI/NIE of the legal representative
Application form for legalization of books (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT asks for additional documentation, provide the Registry certificate and directors' IDs; if book legalization is presented before registration, wait for the Registry's positive note and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Urban, and Environmental Operating Licenses for Recycled Copper Wire Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento (City Council) – Department of Urbanism and Economic Activities; Consejería de Medio Ambiente (Regional Environmental Authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for municipal activity licence (licencia de apertura) and, if required, environmental impact screening (EIA), submitting a technical project, fire safety certificate and occupational risk prevention plan. The municipal authority coordinates with the regional environmental body; operations cannot start until the licence and, when applicable, environmental authorization or EIA pronouncement is granted.
required_dossiers: Licencia de actividad request form
Technical project/memoria signed by a competent technical college
EIA documentation (Annex I or Annex II of Law 21/2013) where capacity thresholds are met
Fire protection certificate issued by competent fire brigade or certified technician
Occupational risk prevention plan and evaluation (Ley 31/1995)
Land-use compatibility certificate (urban qualification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is denied, remedy by revising technical and environmental plans and re-submitting within 30 days; in case of administrative silence, invoke the positive or negative silence provisions under Law 39/2015 and appeal to the administrative jurisdiction if required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria, Comercio y Turismo / Dirección General de Industria y Energía of the relevant Autonomous Community; municipal authority (Ayuntamiento) for the operating activity licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento (municipal industrial activity licence) and, where applicable, Licencia de Actividad Clasificada / Autorización Ambiental Unificada.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agencia de Medio Ambiente – Dirección General de Prevención, Calidad Ambiental y Cambio Climático of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Under Spanish Law 21/2013, a copper scrap recycling facility with non-hazardous waste recovery capacity above 10 t/day requires simplified EIA (Annex II); above 100 t/day requires full EIA (Annex I); storage-only operations below these thresholds require municipal environmental communication (comunicación ambiental).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with RD 815/2013 (Industrial Emissions Directive) and Best Available Techniques reference levels for non-ferrous metal processing: controlled particulate/dust filtration, VOC abatement below applicable ELVs, wastewater pH 6.5-9.5, total suspended solids ≤ 60 mg/l, Cu ≤ 2.0 mg/l; scrap storage and transport in accordance with Law 22/2011 and Regulation (EC) 1013/2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de protección contra incendios (fire safety certificate), structural load inspection certificate for storage racks, loading docks and processing equipment, and occupational health and safety risk assessment under Ley 31/1995, including specific measures for electrical safety, dust, noise, manual handling and machine guarding.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident foreign entities obtain NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by registering with Agencia Tributaria via form submission including incorporation documents, foreign tax ID proof, and Spanish tax representative appointment if lacking permanent establishment. Resident Spanish entities register automatically upon formation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply; tax residency determined by permanent establishment or center of management.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing via Facturae or PEPPOL standards with real-time reporting to AEAT, including digital stamps on invoices and mandatory submission within statutory timelines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to physical exports of goods outside the EU upon proof of removal from EU territory; offshore services zero-rated if provided without Spanish establishment to non-EU clients.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts or refunds if documentation insufficient; penalties up to 200% of tax due plus interest and possible criminal sanctions for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy; the Spanish Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation oversees foreign exchange policy, with operational reporting to the Banco de España's Balance of Payments and Foreign Exchange Division.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange controls restrict profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation for non-resident investors. However, all cross-border payments exceeding €10,000 (or equivalent) must be reported to the Banco de España for statistical and anti-money laundering (AML) purposes. Profit remittances are subject to standard corporate income tax withholding (19% for non-resident entities under the Non-Resident Income Tax Law, unless reduced by a tax treaty) and must be supported by audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates. Capital account transactions (e.g., equity injections, loans) require declaration via the 'Declaración de Operaciones de Inversión Exterior' (Foreign Investment Declaration) to the Ministry of Economy, but prior authorization is not required except for sectors with national security implications (not applicable to scrap metal trading).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds into euros. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts. However, all export receipts must be reported to the Banco de España within 30 days of the transaction date via the 'Declaración de Operaciones de Comercio Exterior' (Foreign Trade Declaration) for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes. The reporting threshold is €12,500 per transaction; cumulative monthly reporting is required for amounts above this threshold. There is no statutory timeline for converting export proceeds to EUR, but companies must maintain documentary evidence (e.g., customs declarations, invoices, SWIFT confirmations) for at least 5 years for AML and tax audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) for daily trade settlements; Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito) for inbound equity injections
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) for trade disbursements; Capital Escrow Account for escrow arrangements
Operational Account (Cuenta de Operaciones) for daily treasury; Capital Escrow Account for project-specific escrow
Operational Account (Cuenta de Negocio) for trade finance; Capital Escrow Account for regulatory deposits
Operational Account (Cuenta de Tesorería) for liquidity management; Capital Escrow Account for investment holding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Spain recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the Spanish Law 21/2011 on Money Creation and Payment Services. EMIs authorized in Spain (e.g., Bnext, N26 Spain) or passporting from other EU/EEA states (e.g., Revolut, Wise) can provide multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment services. However, for a medium-risk sector like recycled scrap metal trading, EMIs may impose lower transaction limits, higher compliance scrutiny, and may not offer documentary credit (LC) facilities. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds for more than 180 days; they are not suitable for escrow or capital injection accounts requiring full banking guarantees. For trade settlements, EMIs are viable for small-value SWIFT transfers but not for large LC transactions. Recommendation: Use a tier-1 bank as primary, with an EMI as a secondary liquidity buffer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial KYC interview for corporate accounts, especially for non-resident directors. Under Spanish AML regulations (Law 10/2010), banks must conduct face-to-face identification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and directors. However, since 2020, remote onboarding via video identification (e.g., using a notary or a certified video call) is permitted if the bank uses a qualified electronic signature and biometric verification. For an SL with non-resident directors, the bank may require at least one director to appear in person at a branch in Spain, or a representative with a notarized power of attorney. For enhanced due diligence (EDD) due to the scrap metal sector, the bank may mandate a physical visit to the company's registered office or warehouse. Practical approach: Engage a Spanish corporate services provider to act as a local agent for KYC, and schedule a physical visit for the managing director to the bank's head office in Madrid or Barcelona.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure: If the company's counterparties or beneficial owners are from jurisdictions on FATF or EU high-risk lists (e.g., certain Latin American or Middle Eastern countries), the bank will trigger enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed corporate structure chart with UBOs and their tax residency; audited financial statements for the last 2 years; contracts with counterparties showing legitimate trade flows; certificates of origin for scrap copper; and a written AML compliance policy. Additionally, obtain a legal opinion from a Spanish law firm confirming the legitimacy of the supply chain and the absence of sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or high-volume transaction patterns (e.g., frequent large wire transfers to non-EU countries without clear commercial rationale).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete trade file for each transaction: purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations (DUA), and proof of payment. Provide a cash flow forecast and explain the commercial cycle (e.g., 30-60 day payment terms). Implement a transaction monitoring system and appoint a compliance officer. Submit a written explanation of the business model to the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between registered business address and actual operations (e.g., no physical presence in Spain).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a lease agreement for a registered office in Spain, or a virtual office with a physical mailbox and a local agent. Submit utility bills, tax registration certificates (CIF), and a letter from the Spanish tax authority (AEAT) confirming tax compliance. If the company is a holding entity, provide a group structure chart and explain the operational role of the Spanish entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital injection (e.g., large equity contribution from a non-resident shareholder).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a bank statement from the shareholder's bank showing the source of funds (e.g., sale of assets, dividends, or loan). Obtain a notarized declaration of the shareholder's wealth and tax residence. Submit a copy of the foreign investment declaration filed with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For loans, provide a loan agreement with commercial terms and evidence of interest rate benchmarking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound capital injections (equity or shareholder loans) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code. For equity contributions, use the purpose code 'G300' (Investment in equity capital) or 'G301' (Investment in shares) under the Spanish Balance of Payments classification. For shareholder loans, use 'G302' (Loans from non-residents). The transfer must be accompanied by a Foreign Investment Declaration (Form DP-2) filed with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs within 30 days of the transaction. The bank will require a copy of the declaration and the underlying corporate resolution. Verification: The bank will verify the UBO and the source of funds; for amounts above €100,000, the bank may request a legal opinion on the investment structure. The funds must be credited to a capital escrow account if the injection is conditional on regulatory approvals (e.g., for a license).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For payments to suppliers of recycled copper wire, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 (wire transfer) for open account transactions, and Documentary Letters of Credit (LC) for larger or riskier transactions. For LC, the bank will issue an MT700 (LC issuance) and MT707 (amendment) via SWIFT. The LC must be irrevocable and confirmed by a reputable bank in the supplier's jurisdiction. For high-value shipments, use a 'Red Clause' LC to allow pre-shipment financing. For payments to EU suppliers, use SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) transfers (MT103 with SEPA format) for instant settlement. For non-EU suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code 'G200' (Payment for goods) and attach the commercial invoice and customs declaration. The bank will require a copy of the bill of lading and the certificate of origin to ensure compliance with EU import regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency Forwards: Over-the-counter (OTC) forward contracts with a Spanish bank or EU-authorized investment firm to lock in exchange rates for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, or EUR/Latin American currencies (e.g., MXN, BRL) for up to 12 months. Requires a master agreement (ISDA or local framework) and collateral.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): For currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., certain Latin American currencies), NDFs are permissible if the underlying trade is in a non-convertible currency. The bank will settle the difference in EUR.

Currency Swaps: Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge both principal and interest on foreign currency loans or trade finance facilities. Permissible under Spanish law, subject to the bank's credit approval and the company's risk management policy.

FX Options: European-style options on major currency pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) to hedge downside risk while retaining upside potential. Requires premium payment and is subject to the bank's derivatives desk approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of annual accounts (aprobación de cuentas anuales) for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting in general assembly; the approved accounts form the basis for registration and filing obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, approved by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting allows any member to request a court to summon the general meeting; resolutions may be challenged; administrators may incur civil liability for losses caused by the delay.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (depósito de cuentas anuales) at the Mercantile Registry, including balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, accounting policies, and auditor's report if audited.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil corresponding to the SL's registered office, with forwarding to the Registro Mercantil Central.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval; for a calendar-year end approved by 30 June, the final deposit deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is blocked from obtaining positive registry certificates and cannot register new corporate deeds until the default is cured; persistent non-filing exposes the company to registry cancellation proceedings, administrative strike-off, and liability of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Modelo 200) declaring taxable results, tax reliefs, and withholding information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year; for a tax year ending 31 December, from 1 July to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges of 10% to 35% of the tax amount plus late-payment interest; specific penalties from EUR 100 to EUR 20,000 depending on the infraction; persistent non-filing can trigger collection enforcement and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership data statement submitted together with the annual accounts deposit to update the Registro de Titularidades Reales.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro Central de Titularidades Reales.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the annual accounts deposit: one month from approval and no later than 31 July for a calendar-year SL.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The annual accounts deposit may be rejected or suspended until a complete beneficial ownership declaration is supplied; failure to comply with anti-money-laundering information duties may result in administrative fines under Law 10/2010 and registry blocks.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory when the SL meets at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Audit is also required for entities forming part of a group subject to audit or when shareholders representing at least 5% of the share capital exercise their statutory right to request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts are prepared under Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007, as amended); consolidated financial statements of groups must apply IFRS as adopted by the European Union in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1606/2002.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership is embedded in the annual accounts deposit form; the SL must complete the prescribed UBO data sheet for the Registro de Titularidades Reales. Any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership must also be recorded in the company's statutory register before relying solely on the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,800 per year for registered office, corporate secretarial, and legal representative services in Spain.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500–12,000 for a small-to-medium SL statutory audit; not charged if the SL qualifies for and validly exercises the audit waiver.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No scrap-sector tax holiday exists for recycled copper wire trading. A newly incorporated Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may apply the 15% reduced corporate income tax rate for the first two tax periods with positive tax base, provided it carries on a genuine economic activity under Art. 29 of Ley 27/2014. General tax credits for R&D, technology innovation, and environmental investments may be available, but none is specific to scrap metal trading.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 — annual Corporate Income Tax return; mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT Sede Electrónica (tax agency online portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; a 31 December year end requires filing by 25 July next year; if the deadline falls on a non-business day, the due date shifts to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period start and end dates, including any short or long period due to incorporation or cessation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Spanish SL tax period. A non-resident shareholder has no entry in this box; only the Spanish entity is the Form 200 filer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, corporate name, legal form (SL), registered office, and type of declaration (individual or consolidated).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the NIF of the Spanish SL. Non-resident parent or shareholder data is not reported on this return unless the SL forms part of a Spanish tax group under Art. 61 LIS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result adjusted to the corporate tax base before loss offset; transfer-pricing and other fiscal adjustments are applied here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Spanish-source income attributable to the SL and the permanent-establishment income if a PE is present. Controlled transactions with non-resident related parties must be reported at arm's-length values, with supporting transfer-pricing documentation available to AEAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings, instalments, and payments on account applied to reduce the final corporate tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Spanish withholding tax borne on gross income paid to the SL. Foreign tax credits are claimed under the relevant DTA and must be supported by certificates of tax residence and fiscal-year documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Differential tax due after credits and instalments, or refundable excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief on dividend, interest, or royalty income is not embedded here; WHT reductions or refunds are processed through Modelo 210 or the dedicated refund procedure after source-level withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers Article 27 LGT recargos: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after more than 12 months, plus late-payment interest. A timely-filed but inaccurate return is subject to the standard late-payment penalty of 50-100% under Article 28 LGT. Failure to file after an AEAT requirement may trigger fixed penalties ranging from EUR 200 to EUR 20,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 — quarterly Corporate Income Tax instalment payment; filed electronically through AEAT Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 20 April, 20 July, 20 October, and 20 December for a 31 December fiscal year; for a non-calendar year end, due within 20 days of the close of each instalment quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF and corporate name of the SL, plus fiscal period of reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL NIF only. Non-resident shareholders do not participate in Modelo 202.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalment calculation method: modalidad de base using the current-year accounting result adjusted per Art. 40 LIS, or modalidad de cuota based on the prior year's tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The calculation must reflect the arm's-length results of the Spanish SL. Transactions with foreign related parties must be included in the cumulative taxable base; no separate non-resident data is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete Modelo 202 filings attract the same Article 27 LGT surcharge schedule and late-payment interest; intentionally incorrect instalments may lead to a penalty reduction in the annual Form 200 assessment and additional interest/surcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish SL applies 19% non-resident withholding tax on qualifying dividends. The non-resident beneficial owner may claim a reduced or zero treaty rate by presenting a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state, together with a declaration of beneficial ownership. Where the reduced rate cannot be applied at source, the excess WHT is recovered through Modelo 210 (non-resident income tax return without permanent establishment) or through the specific refund procedure before AEAT. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the parent must prove a qualifying shareholding and holding period and obtain the EU residence certificate and, when required, the Modelo 211/212annex.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on non-resident royalties and interest is 19% each. EU Interest and Royalties Directive may reduce to 0% for qualifying EU-related companies. Under Spanish income tax treaties, interest is commonly reduced to 0-10% and royalties to 5-15%, subject to TRC and technical/commercial substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 annual net turnover triggers mandatory Master File and Local File obligations under Art. 18 LIS and Royal Decree 634/2015. Simplified documentation is required for smaller entities when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 aggregate in the tax period.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Scope is enforced through the Spanish general anti-abuse rule under Art. 15 LGT, substance-over-form doctrine, CFC rules under Art. 100 LIS, and the Principal Purpose Test applicable under MLI-reformed tax treaties. For a recycled scrap copper wire trader, meaningful personnel, inventory control, negotiation, risk management, and governance decisions must occur in Spain; otherwise AEAT may re-characterise the SL as a conduit, deny DTA benefits, and re-attributed profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-invoicing of export sales, omission of documentary credit or Swift TT proceeds from Form 200, inflating costs with fake supplier invoices, or using shell companies to create fictitious deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-payment penalty of 50% of the underpaid tax, increased to 100% where irregular invoices or obstructive means are used; plus late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal applies when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or allow asset stripping are jointly and severally liable under Art. 42(1)(b) LGT and Art. 43 LGT; criminal conviction triggers personal civil restitution, disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Legal Personality
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no staff, warehouse, customer files, transport arrangements, or commercial decision-making, while routing scrap copper invoicing through Spain to obtain treaty or EU Directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT will re-characterise the transaction under Art. 15 LGT, ignore the sham structure, deny DTA relief, and reassess CIT plus interest. The tax shortfall is subject to the 50-100% penalty scale; fraudulent re-characterisation can also trigger the criminal fraud threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Liability rules allow piercing the corporate veil where the company is a sham; directors face joint liability for unpaid corporate tax and penalties, possible disqualification from conducting business, travel restraints, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud if the concealed amount exceeds EUR 120,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving cash for scrap copper in excess of the Spanish commercial cash threshold (EUR 2,500 per operation, or EUR 1,000 where one counterparty is a non-resident individual), failing to perform customer due diligence on suppliers or buyers, or accepting stolen copper with no traceable origin documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the cash-payment limit under Ley 7/2012 carries a proportional fine of 25% of the transaction amount, with a minimum penalty per infraction; AML violations under Ley 10/2010 can bring fines up to EUR 10 million or 5% of the audited net worth, plus confiscation of illicit proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for failure to implement AML controls; knowingly laundering proceeds of theft or fraud triggers imprisonment under Art. 301 Código Penal, personal fines, and forfeiture of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare Master File/Local File once turnover exceeds EUR 10 million, absence of comparability analysis, undecrypted related-party transactions with the non-resident shareholder or foreign scrap suppliers, or artificial profit shifting through inflated purchase prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust the tax base to arm's length, deny deduction of overstated costs, and apply the 50-100% penalty on the resulting underassessment. Failure to provide required TP documentation triggers specific penalties of EUR 1,500 per data/essential item under Art. 18(13) LIS, with aggregate caps, and may lead to additional negligence penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Administrators who sign transfer-pricing documentation they know to be false are subject to joint liability for the tax debt and penalties under Art. 42/43 LGT; intentional offshore profit-stripping can be prosecuted as tax fraud, resulting in imprisonment and restriction of movement across borders.
